target_customer: Parents in Mexico and Brazil who want to give children an allowance and teach money skills
problem: Parents must choose between giving kids cash or handing over their own cards, and most people in the region lack formal financial education. Mozper offers a kid debit card and app with allowances, spending rules, chores and savings goals.
business_model: Monthly subscription fee per card (reported 69 pesos in Mexico) plus card interchange, B2C2C
product_category: Kids and family fintech, prepaid debit card

founders.name: Gabriel Roizner
previous_startups: Disca (online fashion community, outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page: marketing and product leader with over a decade in fintech and consumer apps across Latin America; managed teams of up to 43. TechCrunch (Aug 2020) says he is based in Miami.

founders.name: Yael Israeli
previous_startups: Boutique finance and strategy consultancy in Panama
founders.background_notes: From the YC page and TechCrunch. Treasurer of the nonprofit Mujeres Brillando per YC page.

founders.name: Pablo Klestorny
founders.background_notes: Named as CTO and co-founder in TechCrunch and in a Latam Fintech article; not listed on the YC page. Described as a longtime tech developer.

competitors.name: Greenlight
competitors.what: US kids debit card and money app that Mozper says it is modeled on
competitors.funding_then: Raised 54 million dollars in 2019 per TechCrunch

competitors.name: GoHenry
competitors.what: UK and US kids debit card and app, named with Greenlight as the incumbent model

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile app on a sponsor bank and card processor (Toka and Visa in Mexico) is standard fintech engineering; the hard parts were licensing partners and compliance, not novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: First mover in Latin America per its pre-seed coverage, but relies on a sponsor bank and the model is copied from Greenlight and GoHenry, so rivals could replicate it.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Neither US incumbent is reported in opened sources to have entered Mexico or Brazil by 2022; Mozper itself expanded to Brazil in January 2022 per search results.

market_need_then: Mozper's YC page says about 70 percent of the region has never received formal financial education and parents in Brazil and Mexico give over 10 billion dollars a year in pocket money, while the only options were cash or lending out an adult card.

branding.name_origin: Co-founder Yael Israeli told TechCrunch the name combines the English words for money, prosperity and Generation Z.

identity.logo: Not confirmed by any source opened
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, reassuring and parent focused, informal address to parents, describing money skills as simple and fun

branding.community_and_virality: Press logos on its site (TechCrunch, Entrepreneur, El Financiero, Expansion) show regional press coverage; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional launch press and a clear story, but no sourced evidence of community, mascot or recognition beyond coverage of funding and launch.

outcome_analysis: Mozper launched in Mexico in late July 2020 and raised a 3.55 million dollar seed in December 2020 led by Hetz, then expanded to Brazil in January 2022. It stayed small at 6 people on the YC page and no later round was found. Reliance on sponsor banks and a niche, regional market make its scale uncertain.
notes: Funding is documented by Crunchbase News (total 5.1M including a 1.6M pre-seed led by Dux, Farrell and Y Combinator), TechCrunch (about 1.5M raised by Aug 2020) and Latam Fintech (770K pre-seed, Mar 2020); amounts differ because of tranches, so the 770K round is recorded and the remainder to 1.6M is an unrecorded tranche. Business Wire and Fintech Futures returned 403. A search summary says the card network moved to Mastercard in Brazil, unverified. YC page lists founding as 2019. No source found for current status after 2022.
